evidence_limits: No Search Console, keyword tool or paid dataset was available. Every keyword choice is a qualitative hypothesis about search intent, not evidence of volume, difficulty, traffic or ranking.

Web research used 12 standard web searches on 2026-10-22. Third-party pages were NOT opened: this environment's network policy rejected direct connections (proxy 403 on CONNECT) and the fetch tool could not resolve external hosts. Third-party sources are therefore recorded as search_result_snippet_only, meaning the search tool's summary of result snippets. Treat any figure from them as unverified.

Two primary sources for the captions brief (W3C WAI captions page and YouTube Help answer 2734796) were read by the parent session on 2026-10-22 and supplied as verified summaries; they are marked primary_source_summary_read_by_parent_2026-10-22, not as pages this session fetched. TechSmith's tutorial page could not be read by either session.

Rollside pages (home, /prompter/, /support/, /support/prompter/, /camera/, /mac/, /support/mac/, /about/, /blog/, sitemap) were fetched and read directly on 2026-10-22. The App Store listing and support.rollside.studio were blocked and were not read.
Search results seen for a topic show that competing pages exist and how they frame the question. They do not show how many people search for it.
Product status changes. Every author must recheck the claims_to_recheck list against live Rollside pages on the day of writing.

posts.title: How to write a video hook when it is just you talking to camera
posts.primary_keyword: how to write a video hook
related_keywords: first three seconds of a video
posts.intent: Informational / how-to. Reader question: what should I say in the first sentence so people keep watching, when I have no b-roll or flashy edit to lean on?
posts.angle: Hooks for a face and a voice only. The promise is a method for writing several candidate openers for one video and choosing the one that is easiest to say and clearest about the payoff, rather than a list of 50 formula templates. Differs from the 60-second script post, which trims an opening for length; this post decides what the opening should be in the first place. Differs from the writing post, which covers voice and breath across the whole script.
outline: Why a talking head hook has to work with the sound off and on: first frame, first words
Write five openers before you write the rest: question, plain promise, mistake, surprising detail, named viewer
Score them by saying them aloud: can you deliver it in one breath and does it name the payoff?
Make the second sentence keep the promise, so the hook is not a bait and switch
posts.example_brief: Hypothetical: a potter filming why mugs crack in the kiln. Show five draft openers for the same video, read each aloud, and explain why two are rejected (vague, takes two breaths) and which one is kept. Label all openers as written for the example; no claims about retention.
posts.natural_writing_notes: Open with one of the bad openers, not a definition of a hook. Use a short annotated list for the five openers, then prose for the judgement. Avoid percentages about viewer drop-off unless a source has been read and cited.
posts.product_cta: Light: load the chosen opener at the top of a Prompter script and rehearse just the first line until it sounds like speech. Link to /prompter/.
claims_to_recheck: Prompter availability and free tier on /prompter/
Any platform behaviour mentioned (autoplay with sound off) must be framed generally or sourced

posts.title: How to stop saying um on camera without sounding scripted
posts.primary_keyword: how to stop saying um on camera
posts.intent: Problem-solving. Reader question: I watch my footage back and hear um, so, like everywhere. How do I cut them down without reading every word?
posts.angle: Treats fillers as a planning problem, not a willpower problem: most appear at transitions and openings, so plan those moments. Accepts that some fillers are normal and that editing can remove a few. Differs from the reading-naturally post, which is about prompter eyeline and expression, not unscripted speech.
outline: Find your pattern: record two minutes unscripted and mark where the fillers cluster
Plan the joins: write out openings and transitions, leave the middle in bullets
Swap the filler for a pause and practise the silence
Slow the start, and decide which fillers can stay or be cut in the edit
posts.example_brief: Hypothetical 20-second transcript of someone explaining how to choose a yoga mat, with each filler bolded and a note on where it falls (start, between points, before a number). Then the same passage with planned transition lines and marked pauses. State clearly that the transcript is invented for illustration and that no counts are measured results.
posts.natural_writing_notes: Use an annotated transcript as the centrepiece. Avoid the cliché that fillers 'destroy credibility'. If citing advice that a speech-language therapist may help for non-habit causes, keep it brief and non-diagnostic.
posts.product_cta: Light: a script with written transitions and bullet points can sit in Prompter; Voice follow pauses when you stop speaking, which makes a deliberate silence easier to practise. Recheck requirements.
claims_to_recheck: Voice follow pause behaviour and requirements (iOS 18+, supported device, on-device language)
Prompter shows text only; does not record

posts.title: How to write a tutorial video script people can actually follow
posts.primary_keyword: how to write a tutorial video script
posts.intent: Informational / how-to with template. Reader question: how do I script a step-by-step video so viewers can follow along without rewinding?
posts.angle: Writing for someone who is doing the task while watching: a two-column say / show script, one action per line, checkpoints that tell viewers what they should see before moving on. Differs from the general writing post, which is about sounding like yourself; this is about sequence, visuals and viewer success.
outline: Start from the finished result and the viewer's starting point
Build the two-column script: what you say, what the camera shows
One action per line, with a checkpoint after each step
Warn before the common mistake, not after
Rehearse with your hands, not just your voice
posts.example_brief: Hypothetical: a tutorial on replacing a bike inner tube. Show a short two-column excerpt for three steps, including one checkpoint ('you should be able to see the valve straight up') and one advance warning. Clearly labelled as an illustrative script, not a tested repair guide; keep technical steps general and correct.
posts.natural_writing_notes: Use a fenced plain-text block for the two-column excerpt (HTML is escaped and tables may not render; check the renderer before using a markdown table). Vary paragraph length; one short checklist only.
posts.product_cta: Light: keep the 'say' column in Prompter and use page jumps or a remote to move between steps while your hands are busy. Recheck remote support wording.
